edit.why.q: What can a value hold, and what do encrypting and metadata do?
edit.why.a: A value is saved exactly as typed, line breaks included. Encrypting happens in this browser; tools then need the password. Metadata is not encrypted.
value.why.q: How is the value read, and what about encrypted values?
value.why.a: The value is read only when you press the eye or Copy; hiding it or closing the entry clears it. An encrypted value's password stays in this browser.
faq.vaultFor.a: Values your tools and agents read by name: tokens, passwords, settings. Add a value your tools or agents should read by name; you can encrypt it with a password first. The list does not show values. In an entry, the value is read only when you press the eye or Copy, and is removed from the page when you hide it or close the entry.
faq.scope.q: What is the difference between Global and a realm's entries?
faq.scope.a: Global entries are shared by every realm and by tools that run without one. The entries of a realm belong to that realm. The same name in another realm, or in Global, is a different entry. Pick a realm from the realm menu at the top to see its own entries (on a phone, tap the realm square).
faq.showValue.q: How do I see or copy a value?
faq.showValue.a: Open the entry and press the eye to show the value, or Copy to copy it without showing it. The value is read only then. Hiding it or closing the entry removes it from this page; the next press reads it again. An encrypted value asks for its password first; the password never leaves this browser. JSON values are shown formatted, with Raw for the exact text; Copy always copies the exact text, not the formatted view; for an encrypted entry that is the decrypted value. You can also show the encrypted form, to paste where a tool expects it.
faq.encrypt.q: What does "Encrypt with a password" do?
faq.encrypt.a: The value is encrypted in this browser before it is sent, and tools need the password to read it. To open an encrypted value here, enter its password; the password never leaves this browser. An entry shown as "Not marked" has no encryption recorded. To protect its value, use Replace value and tick Encrypt with a password. The Hoody SDK, CLI and agent use the same encrypted form, so they can read it with the password.
faq.valueInput.q: What can I put in a name and a value?
faq.valueInput.a: A name uses letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 100 characters. Names starting with "hoody." belong to Hoody's own tools. A value is hidden as you type; use the eye to check it. Line breaks are kept, so you can paste a whole key or certificate. It is saved exactly as typed, unless you encrypt it. Replacing a value overwrites the old one, and the old value is not shown here.
faq.metadata.a: Metadata is your own details kept with the entry, as a JSON object such as {"source": "ci"}. It is not encrypted. When you replace a value, the entry keeps its metadata unless you tick Change metadata. With it on, saving replaces the entry's metadata, and an empty field removes it all. The names "encrypted" and "write_id" are kept by the Hub; use other names.
faq.export.a: Export saves the readable entries of the vault shown (a realm's or Global's), with their names, values and metadata, in one file. Encrypted, the default, locks values that are not already encrypted with a password you choose; a value that is already encrypted keeps its own password. Names and metadata stay readable. Readable saves values as stored, so anyone with the file can read the ones that are not encrypted; the Hub asks you to confirm first. An entry that could not be read or was removed is left out, and the Hub tells you before you save.
faq.export.a.terminal: Export saves a file to your device, so it is only in the web Hub. Open the Vault there to export.

import.st.held: Not sent: a change is held
